scope: Six selected primary references: four 2025–2026 MI-EEG DG papers and two foundations. This is a targeted novelty check, not a systematic review.

references.title: Supervised Contrastive Learning-Based Domain Generalization Network for Cross-Subject Motor Decoding
references.date_note: 2025 issue; DOI includes 2024 because of advance publication.
references.relevance: Source-only generalization through supervised contrastive class regularization and correlation alignment. It establishes that source-only/class-invariant MI learning is prior art.
references.verification_scope: Crossref publisher-deposited bibliographic fields verified. Primary abstract/proceedings search inspected; publisher full text not inspected.

references.title: EEG-DG: A Multi-Source Domain Generalization Framework for Motor Imagery EEG Classification
references.venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
references.date_note: 2025 issue; DOI includes 2024 because of advance publication.
references.relevance: Multi-source MI EEG domain generalization with source marginal and conditional distribution alignment; motivates comparison against existing DG ideas rather than a first-ever claim.
references.verification_scope: Crossref metadata and PubMed abstract/author list inspected; author preprint link supplied, not a reproduced implementation.

references.title: MI-DGHCL: Motor imagery EEG domain generalization via hyperbolic contrastive learning
references.relevance: MI EEG domain generalization combining feature consistency and hyperbolic contrastive learning. Consistency and invariance alone do not establish novelty for this project.
references.verification_scope: Crossref metadata and primary publisher indexed abstract inspected. Publisher page returned HTTP 403 in direct access; full text and code not inspected.

references.title: Cross-Subject Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram Decoding with Domain Generalization
references.relevance: MI EEG DG using spectral knowledge distillation, correlation alignment and distance regularization; directly relevant prior art for any spectral-consistency claim.
references.verification_scope: Crossref metadata and primary publisher indexed abstract inspected. Direct MDPI page rate limited and PMC presented an access challenge; no full-text access claim.

references.title: Distributionally Robust Neural Networks for Group Shifts: On the Importance of Regularization for Worst-Case Generalization
references.date_note: ICLR 2020 publication; arXiv first submission 2019. The ICLR page uses the shortened title Distributionally Robust Neural Networks; the full paper title is taken from the author preprint.
references.relevance: Group-DRO is established prior art. It is the direct robust-risk baseline; early stopping and regularization matter for worst-group generalization.
references.verification_scope: Official ICLR abstract/author list and author arXiv title/author/version metadata inspected. No conference DOI identified; the given DOI explicitly identifies the preprint.

references.title: Optimization of conditional value-at-risk
references.date_note: Foundational method reference, outside the 2024–2026 MI literature window.
references.relevance: Upper-tail loss objectives are established. The discrete minibatch group top-half mean in this proposal is not a new CVaR theory or a population-risk guarantee.
references.verification_scope: Publisher-deposited Crossref title/authors/year/volume/issue/pages/DOI verified. Author publication list inspected; no full-text verification claimed.
